item.title: Like and as at the maker festival
item.explanation_text:
Use like before a noun phrase to show that two people or things are similar in some way. In a note to volunteers, “The paper lantern opens like an umbrella” compares the way the two objects open. Use as before a noun phrase to name someone’s actual role or explain what something is used for. In “I’m here as a guide,” guide is your role. In “We use a toolbox lid as a tray,” the lid has the function of a tray during the activity.

Use as before a clause to show how to do something. “Set up the stand as the diagram shows” tells volunteers to follow the diagram. In “Do as shown,” as shown is a shorter form of as it is shown. In informal conversation, you may also hear like before a clause, as in “Set it up like I showed you.” For the written festival instructions in this lesson, choose as before a clause that tells someone how to do a task.
item.contrast_text: “She works as a guide” names her actual job. “She speaks like a guide” compares the way she speaks with the way a guide speaks. “She speaks as the trainer showed her” says she follows the trainer’s example.
item.common_error_pattern: Using like to name an assigned role or function, or using as before a noun phrase when the intended meaning is a simple comparison.

examples.bad: I’m on duty like a safety checker. (My assigned role is safety checker.)
examples.good: I’m on duty as a safety checker.

examples.bad: The thin metal strip bends as a spring. (The strip bends in a similar way to a spring.)
examples.good: The thin metal strip bends like a spring.

examples.bad: This wooden crate serves like a seat. (The crate is the seat at this station.)
examples.good: This wooden crate serves as a seat.

examples.bad: Join the two parts as the label show.
examples.good: Join the two parts as the label shows.

children.title: Write a volunteer badge
children.instructions: Choose exactly one word, like or as. The badge states Nina’s assigned role. Write only the missing word.

children.title: Describe a test sound
children.instructions: Choose exactly one word, like or as. The note compares the sound of the motor to the sound of an insect. Write only the missing word.
children.prompt_text: The tiny motor buzzes ___ a bee.

children.title: Label a paint station
children.instructions: Choose exactly one word, like or as. The bottle cap holds paint at the station. Write only the missing word.
children.prompt_text: At this station, the bottle cap serves ___ a paint cup.

children.title: Complete a cutting guide
children.instructions: Choose exactly one word, like or as. Follow the written instruction pattern “Do as the video shows.” Write only the missing word.
children.prompt_text: Cut the corners ___ the template shows.

children.title: Describe the prize draw
children.instructions: Choose exactly one word, like or as. The note compares the shape of the tickets to the shape of leaves. Write only the missing word.
children.prompt_text: The prize tickets are shaped ___ oak leaves.

children.title: Correct the shift roster
children.instructions: Omar’s assigned job is ticket collector. Replace one word to make the sentence state his role. Keep all the other words and write the full sentence.
children.prompt_text: Omar is working like a ticket collector on the afternoon shift.
accepted_answers: Omar is working as a ticket collector on the afternoon shift.

children.title: Edit a robot demo caption
children.instructions: The toy robot’s movement is similar to a penguin’s. Replace one word to make the comparison clear. Keep all the other words and write the full sentence.
children.prompt_text: The toy robot walks as a penguin.
accepted_answers: The toy robot walks like a penguin.

children.title: Rewrite a note about sound
children.instructions: Start with “The pump sounds” and end with “a drum.” Join those parts with the word like. Write one sentence.
children.prompt_text: The pump makes a sound similar to a drum.
accepted_answers: The pump sounds like a drum.

children.title: Record what a spare box is for
children.instructions: Start with “We used the spare box,” add as, and finish with “a footrest.” Write one sentence.
children.prompt_text: We put our feet on the spare box to rest them.
accepted_answers: We used the spare box as a footrest.

children.title: Combine two sticker instructions
children.instructions: Start with “Place the stickers.” Add as followed by “the sample shows.” Write one sentence.
children.prompt_text: Place the stickers. Follow the sample.
accepted_answers: Place the stickers as the sample shows.

children.title: Assemble a handover note
children.instructions: Put the tiles in order to report a role at the tool desk. Start with “This morning,” and use each tile once.
children.prompt_text: at the tool desk. / as / This morning, / the shift leader / Hana worked
accepted_answers: This morning, Hana worked as the shift leader at the tool desk.

children.title: Arrange a wire-clip instruction
children.instructions: Put the tiles in order to tell a volunteer how to attach a clip. Start with “Attach the wire clip” and use each tile once.
children.prompt_text: shown / Attach the wire clip / on the instruction card. / as
accepted_answers: Attach the wire clip as shown on the instruction card.
